transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-07
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alex Fisher, Priya Shah, Maya Ortiz (Redwood) — Mark Ramirez, Laura Chen, Ethan Park, Sophie Lane (Cobalt)

Summary: quick renewal + expansion chat: Cobalt wants to upgrade reserved capacity, add EU region, and discuss contract extension/term and procurement timeline. Also asked for updated pricing and security docs; Redwood to run dedicated benchmarks and share SOC2/KMS docs.

[00:00] Alex Fisher: hey everyone, thanks for joining — apprec appreciate you taking the time, i'll kick off — agenda is quick renewal check and the expansion ask into EU that Mark sent over.
[00:18] Mark Ramirez: yep thanks Alex, high level — we've been happy with reliability but traffic has grown ~3x q/q, and we hit scaling limits last Friday — so main ask is more reserved capacity and adding an eu region to reduce latency for EMEA users.
[00:35] Priya Shah: thanks Mark, can you give a sense of current qps and peak seq lengths, and which models you're serving? that'll help frame the sizing.
[00:48] Laura Chen: sure, right now approx 120 rps average, peaks at ~480 rps for short-form prompts, seqs usually 512 tokens — we're running a fine-tuned open-architecture model (labelled internally as cobalt-base-ft) for routing and auth decisions; want better p95 latency <120ms.
[01:05] Ethan Park: also for infra side we need region isolation — EU-residency for some customers plus separate key management. we currently host in us-west only.
[01:20] Alex Fisher: makes sense. for capacity we typically recommend reserved pools for predictable throughput — we talked about 3x reserved as an option in the renewal. that would give headroom for the next 12 months and better unit costs.
[01:36] Mark Ramirez: that's the direction we want. can you break down delta cost vs hosted bursts? procurement will ask for concrete numbers.
[01:45] Priya Shah: absolutely — Alex i'll include a per-token and per-hour breakdown in the quote. also we should validate p95 latency on dedicated pool — we'll run a benchmark with your PoC dataset.
[02:00] Laura Chen: on the model side, we might switch to a quantized variant in EU for cost; will that require any special work for KV cache or tokenization differences?
[02:13] Priya Shah: good question — quantized model variants are supported, but we recommend a short compatibility test. KV cache behavior is consistent but we do need to confirm kernel selection for the quantized path; i'll include that in the bench plan.
[02:30] Sophie Lane: from procurement perspective: term length? we're considering a 12-month commit but want a 6-month review clause and ability to increase capacity mid-term. also need SSO/SAML, audit logs, and encryption at rest with customer KMS.
[02:46] Maya Ortiz: we can support SSO/SAML and provide audit log exports; KMS integration is supported for Private deployments and Dedicated via BYOK — we'll share the integration guide and SOC2 docs after the call.
[03:00] Ethan Park: is the KMS flow the same for hosted dedicated? we need HSM or customer-managed keys for EU data.
[03:10] Alex Fisher: the Dedicated offering supports customer KMS — technically we have two flows: hosted with Redwood-managed keys and dedicated with customer-managed KMS/HSM — i'll have Maya attach the architecture notes.
[03:24] Mark Ramirez: what's the SLA if we move to dedicated? last time there was mention of an SLA-backed latency target.
[03:32] Priya Shah: Dedicated includes a throughput SLA and uptime SLA — for latency we provide observed p95 SLO and can configure fallback policies to a cheaper model if capacity is saturated. we'll document the exact numbers in the quote and SLO appendix.
[03:49] Laura Chen: want to test failover behavior — if the dedicated pool is saturated can we fail to a lower-cost model without breaking pipeline? e.g., preserve response structure.
[03:59] Priya Shah: yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants; part of the bench we'll run a controlled saturation test and validate structured output compatibility.
[04:15] Mark Ramirez: timeline: procurement needs a number to review this month. can we get a revised quote and legal redline window?
[04:22] Alex Fisher: we can get the quote out within 3 business days and target contract redlines within two weeks. Sophie, does that align?
[04:30] Sophie Lane: yes, if we get pricing and contract by 10/10 we'll route internally.
[04:38] Priya Shah: i'll book the benchmark slot — need PoC dataset and expected load profile; Mark/Laura can you send that by monday?
[04:46] Laura Chen: we'll send sample traces and a 48-hour spike profile by monday morning.
[04:52] Maya Ortiz: i'll DM the secure doc links for SOC2 and KMS guide; Alex will attach the updated quote and SLO appendix.
[04:59] Mark Ramirez: one more thing — EU region: do you support GDPR data residency and separate audit trail per region? some customers require per-tenant residency.
[05:10] Alex Fisher: yes, we can provision a VPC-based EU region under Dedicated or Private, and we can enable per-region audit logs. Maya will include the details and any limitations.
[05:22] Ethan Park: on network: do you support private peering or interconnect to our cloud provider in eu-west-1?
[05:29] Priya Shah: we do support direct peering and private connectivity for Dedicated — we'll map options depending on your cloud.
[05:36] Sophie Lane: any blockers on our side for the 12-month extension if we get numbers? legal typically wants more clarity on termination clauses and rate increases year 2.
[05:45] Alex Fisher: understood — we'll propose a 12-month term with a 6-month review clause and explicit headroom increase options; we'll call out any price change mechanics in year 2.
[05:59] Mark Ramirez: ok sounds good. appreciate the responsiveness.
[06:05] Alex Fisher: recap: Redwood will send revised quote for 3x reserved capacity + EU region pricing, Priya will run dedicated benchmarks with PoC dataset, Maya will share SOC2/KMS/audit docs, Sophie will send redlines, and we'll schedule legal sync next week. any last items?
[06:20] Laura Chen: please include expected token unit costs for quantized vs full-precision models in the quote.
[06:27] Priya Shah: will do — include estimated per-token cost and expected p95 delta.
[06:33] Alex Fisher: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email with links and next steps.

Notes: transcription contains minor recognition errors — product names sometimes mistranscribed (e.g., 'kv cache' as 'k v cache'), occasional dropped punctuation. References to internal model names are customer-provided.

References/attachments mentioned on call:
- Renewal quote (to be sent)
- SOC2 report + KMS integration guide (link to secure share)
- Benchmark plan spreadsheet (Redwood to create)

End of transcript.
